title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" and a deterministic rule-based validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The validator flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111 and the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, a concise clarification of provider-audit bookkeeping, artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to convert operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Production safety requires that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, command-order workflows, and higher-order policy invariants. A common mitigation architecture in recent proposals is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this architectural trend and argue that layered V&V reduces risk [1]–[3]. However, there is little large-scale, preregistered, paired evidence quantifying the marginal value contributed uniquely by a sandboxed-emulation stage when a strong deterministic validator is already present.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? We contribute (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution, (2) a paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting, (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation that explains a near-zero marginal effect in this regime, and (4) reproducibility guidance and prescriptive boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent survey and architectural reports summarize the practical trend of combining LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]. Configuration-analysis tools and emulation-based validation are common in NetOps research prototypes and are invoked when static rule-sets cannot capture dynamic, stateful device behavior [2]. Prototype integrations report heterogeneous gains: in some task regimes a verifier alone catches most dangerous errors, while in others emulation uncovers subtle runtime failures that static checks miss [3]. These prior findings motivated a paired design that isolates downstream guarded-stage signals by reusing identical initial candidates across the two conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) with a preregistered minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20. Inclusion/exclusion, deterministic reseed rules for parser failures, multiplicity handling for exploratory comparisons, and contamination controls were fixed prior to execution.

Task bank, topology templates, and vendor abstraction. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair task family. The bank covers three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest entry contains initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) with archived model configuration. Per the preregistration we enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair exactly one sampled initial candidate was obtained and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions. This isolates any between-condition discordance to downstream guarded-stage observations or to repair-stage activity.

Baseline validator specification. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based engine that performs vendor-CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, workflow/atomicity constraints (e.g., make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change), protected-interface invariants, group activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The validator emits a binary detection flag under the full_intent_constraint_validation scoring rule and produces a validator_trace (validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes) for every evaluated candidate.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed emulation harness. The guarded pipeline applies the baseline validator and then executes the same candidate in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes the normalized CLI sequence against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulator records runtime observations (interface transition sequences, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, and topological reachability). Emulation observations are mapped to runtime-observation rules that can trigger a guarded detection if they reveal policy or safety violations not encoded in the static validator. The emulation-to-detection mapping is intentionally conservative for this study: it flags only runtime behaviors that concretely violate stated workflow policies.

Clarification of provider-call audit bookkeeping. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation include a provider-call audit that reports stage-level counts. In that bookkeeping "shared_initial_generation" counts the single provider calls that produced the shared sampled candidate for each pair, while an additional "repair" or other guarded-stage label counts any extra model invocations performed only in the guarded pipeline (e.g., an allowed repair call). Thus the manifest-level accounting can legitimately show a dominant count in the "shared" class (720) and a small number in the guarded-stage class (1) when exactly one repair call occurred across the run. These recorded stage-level counts do not imply duplicate independent candidate generations were performed for paired comparisons—the preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract prevented that.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory statistics (artifact-grounded). Complete pair accounting: complete_pair_count = 720. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected-by-both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values reported here are taken directly from the archived analysis artifacts.

Run accounting and repair attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 (stage breakdown: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1). Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single discordant n10 entry must be attributable either to (i) a guarded-emulation observation not codified in the validator, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The archived per-episode records contain the pair_id and the validator_trace and repair trace for that unique discordant episode, allowing an auditor to inspect whether the guarded detection arose from emulation-only observation or from the documented repair-stage call. (We omit raw transcripts and per-file hashes from the paper; the execution manifest in the archival bundle identifies the canonical raw-results file for detailed inspection.)

Representative diagnostics. Representative scoring traces show that most shared_initial candidates complied with validator rule-sets (validator_trace.violation_count = 0 in the majority of exemplars) and that sandboxed emulation corroborated static checks for the curated task bank. Those representative artifacts illustrate the validator’s coverage of the workflow patterns embedded in the deterministic generator (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change).
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage marginal benefit was negligible. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the near-zero aggregate effect in this experimental regime.

Validator ceiling and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encoded the syntactic and workflow checks exercised by the curated task generator. The high baseline success rate (719/720) leaves essentially no headroom for the guarded stage to flag additional failures in this constrained regime.

Curated, parser-validated task bank. Confirmatory items were included only after deterministic parser acceptance; this reduces both syntactic noise and adversarial inputs, concentrating the bank where a strong validator can achieve high coverage. Deterministic reconciliation confirms zero irrecoverable parser exclusions for the confirmatory set.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Reusing the same sampled candidate isolates downstream causes of discordance to guarded-stage observations or repair calls. The provider-call audit shows a single repair-stage invocation across the run, and that single invocation corresponds to the unique guarded-only detection (n10 = 1). Together these factors produce a narrowly scoped, artifact-grounded near-zero marginal effect.

Operational implications and conditional boundary claims. For operator pipelines that enforce parser-level prevalidation and deploy high-coverage static validators tailored to expected intent patterns, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide negligible incremental detection benefit at scale. This is a conditional finding: in noisier, adversarial, multi-vendor, or stateful production regimes—conditions underrepresented in our curated bank—sandboxed emulation is more likely to surface runtime-only faults and thus remain operationally valuable.

Recommendations. (i) Where low latency and throughput are priorities and input intents are well constrained, invest in richer static validators to capture workflow constraints. (ii) Use guarded sandboxing selectively for high-impact or high-risk changes where emulation fidelity matters. (iii) Develop adversarial/fuzzing task banks to find validator coverage gaps; our archived representative traces can seed such efforts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmed study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping. We interpret this result as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding driven by validator ceiling effects and a curated, parser-validated task design. Generalization to adversarial or production-like regimes requires targeted extensions (adversarial tasks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation) that the archived bundle can help bootstrap.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task bank and parser-based inclusion reduce ecological diversity and produce a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisy, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit cross-model and cross-validator generalizability.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contributions but remove any potential between-condition generation variability (e.g., independent re-generation benefits for the guarded pipeline).
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity is limited by the harness used; higher-fidelity vendor-/OS-specific emulators or long-lived control-plane modeling could alter outcomes in other regimes.

Power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) is far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation and auditing; these uncertainties are documented in the archived execution manifest.
